info.name: Job Portal Backend API
info.description:
Complete test suite for the Job Portal REST API (Node.js + Express + MongoDB).

HOW TO RUN
1. Start MongoDB and the API (`npm run seed` once, then `npm run dev`).
2. Import this file into Postman.
3. Open the collection > Variables and set `jwtSecret` to the JWT_SECRET from your .env (only needed by the 'Expired token' request) and check `adminEmail` / `adminPassword`.
4. Click Run collection and run everything IN ORDER (folders 00 to 08). Authentication is an httpOnly cookie, which Postman's cookie jar stores and re-sends automatically; each folder starts by logging in as the role it needs.

Every request has automated tests (Tests tab).

item.name: 02 - No Auth & Invalid Token
Logout (clear any cookie left over from before)

request.description: Makes sure the cookie jar is empty so the next requests are truly unauthenticated.
Sends a garbage JWT in the cookie header.

exec: const payload = b64url(JSON.stringify({ id: pm.variables.get('jobSeekerId'), iat: now - 7200, exp: now - 3600 }));
pm.request.headers.upsert({ key: 'Cookie', value: 'token=' + header + '.' + payload + '.' + sig });

request.description: Needs the collection variable `jwtSecret` to equal JWT_SECRET in your .env. The script signs a token that expired an hour ago.

item.description: Requests that must be rejected because there is no cookie, or the cookie is bad.

exec: pm.test("Job belongs to the logged in employer", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.job.employer).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("employerId")); });
pm.test("Skills are normalised to lower case", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.job.requiredSkills).to.include("node.js"); });
pm.test("Validation errors are listed", function () { const j = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(j.errors).to.be.an("array").that.is.not.empty; });

request.description: Bad title/description/location, unknown employment type, salary max < min, empty skills, deadline in the past.

exec: pm.test("Contains the job I created", function () { const ids = pm.response.json().data.jobs.map(j => j._id); pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("jobId")); });
pm.test("Employer info is public-safe (no email)", function () { const e = pm.response.json().data.job.employer; pm.expect(e).to.not.have.property("email"); });
pm.test("Validation errors are listed", function () { const j = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(j.errors).to.be.an("array").that.is.not.empty; });
